notes.A: The decorator names every fixture, but I had to match each key back to a parameter in a different line, and the step from a Database fixture to a Tx parameter is never shown.
notes.B: The only style where the line tells the whole story, use(tx, source) shows both the database and the wrapper, after one look at sketch.py:use's two-argument form.
notes.C: Slowest: an alias (SourceTx) hides a NewType, which hides a fixture found only by scanning return types, and plain DbTx leaves the subtype match ambiguous.
notes.D: Inline use_any(source) reads quickly per parameter, but the Database-to-Tx step is hidden and Any throws away the type check.
notes.E: Every fixture is named on its parameter, but Annotated[..., From(...)] triples the line length and the Tx step is still implicit.
notes.F: Tx[SourceDb] names the role right in the type, which helps for c1/c5/c6, but plain Tx[Database] in c2-c4 says nothing and its match to a fixture is ambiguous.
notes.G: Shortest explicit form, = source reads at a glance, though it looks like an ordinary default argument and hides the Tx step.
notes.H: Familiar pytest-style name matching, but the line says nothing, so every parameter needs a trip to fixtures.py, and the c7 override changes the meaning silently.
